en: Mount Mayon in Albay features a perfectly symmetrical volcanic cone that is easily observable from the city of Legazpi.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical grass-covered mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
Taal Volcano in Batangas displays a unique nested geological structure with a crater lake containing the small Vulcan Point island.
Mount Pulag in Benguet features a distinct mossy forest zone where tree trunks are completely covered in thick, damp moss.
The white sand beaches of Boracay in Aklan are composed primarily of finely crushed coral and shell fragments.
El Nido in Palawan features towering, vertical limestone karst cliffs that rise directly out of the clear turquoise seawater.
During the amihan season, the Philippines experiences cool northeast monsoon winds bringing observable dry weather to most of the country.
Mount Apo in Davao features observable hot springs and sulfur vents near its summit, indicating its active geothermal nature.
The Puerto Princesa Underground River in Palawan flows through massive, dark limestone caves before emptying directly into the sea.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao showcase massive, stepped agricultural landscapes visibly carved into the steep mountains over two millennia ago.
The islands of Romblon are geologically famous for their extensive, observable coastal outcrops of high-quality, polished white marble rock.
The coral reefs of Apo Island in Negros Oriental display vibrant, easily observable marine biodiversity just below the ocean surface.
